tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should accept object handle as an argument
[jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should accept object handle to primitive types
[jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should warn about recursive objects
[jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should accept object handle to unserializable value
[jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should use the same JS wrappers
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.getProperty should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.jsonValue should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.jsonValue works with jsonValues that are not objects
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.jsonValue works with jsonValues that are primitives
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.jsonValue should work with dates
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.jsonValue should not throw for circular objects
reason: Creates a handle with `page.evaluateHandle` (or `handle.evaluateHandle`, or passes one back into `page.evaluate`), which runs in the isolated world, and stock WebKit has no isolated worlds (`isolatedWorlds` is unsupported), so it fails `Unsupported` there

tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle Page.evaluateHandle should return the RemoteObject
reason: Reads `remoteObject()`, which returns the Chrome DevTools Protocol's `Runtime.RemoteObject` for the handle, a protocol detail Strider's handles don't expose

tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.getProperties should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.getProperties should return even non-own properties
reason: Listing a handle's properties as handles with `getProperties()`, a map of them; Strider's JSHandle has `evaluate`, `evaluateHandle`, `read` and `release`, and no property enumeration

tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.asElement should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.asElement should return null for non-elements
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.asElement should return ElementHandle for TextNodes
decision: Playwright is evidence, not the template
reason: Casts a JSHandle to an ElementHandle with `asElement`, which is null for a non-element and an element handle for a node, including a text node. Strider's JSHandle has no cast, so each test's first step has no counterpart

tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.toString should work for primitives
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.toString should work for complicated objects
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.toString should work with different subtypes
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.toString should work with window subtypes
reason: Asserts the text a JS handle's `toString()` gives for what it holds (`JSHandle:2`, `JSHandle@window`, `JSHandle@map`). Strider's JSHandle has no string preview: it reads its value with `read` and evaluates with `evaluate`. No matrix row covers a handle's string form; `method-locator-tostring`, the same preview missing on a locator, is the nearest

tests: [jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle[Symbol.dispose] should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle[Symbol.asyncDispose] should work
[jshandle.test] JSHandle JSHandle.move should work
reason: Disposes a handle with JavaScript's `using`, `await using`, or `move()`, which transfers it to a new handle. Strider's JSHandle has `release` and no disposal protocol, and handles are released with their scope; the matrix row for the disposal protocol is the nearest
